entities.name: Methyl ester hydrolysis
observations: Decoded reactant is COC(=O)Ar, while decoded product is OC(=O)Ar.
Formula changes from C25H23N3O2 to C24H21N3O2, consistent with methyl ester deprotection/hydrolysis to a carboxylic acid.
The heteroaromatic scaffold is represented with a different tautomer or atom ordering in the product; no new carbon framework is required.

entities.name: Aqueous base hydrolysis
observations: Plausible conditions are LiOH, NaOH, or KOH in aqueous alcohol or THF/water, followed by acidic workup.
These conditions commonly convert methyl esters to carboxylic acids without changing a stable heteroaromatic scaffold.

entities.name: Acidic ester hydrolysis
observations: Alternative conditions are aqueous HCl or H2SO4, optionally in methanol, ethanol, dioxane, or water, followed by neutralization.
Acid hydrolysis is plausible but generally less preferred than mild base when the heteroaromatic ring is acid-sensitive.
